confidence_notes: I used web searches for the food and drink prices. Several crowd-sourced cost-of-living sites (Numbeo, Expatica, Hikersbay, averagecostof.living) broadly agree on the restaurant prices. A cappuccino is about $5 to $6, a pint of domestic draft beer is about $6.40 to $7, an inexpensive meal is about $20, and a three-course meal for two is about $75 to $99. Those four anchors are medium-high confidence, although the sources were captured at different dates around mid-2026. Cocktail and wine are less certain. The only cocktail figure found was a thin Expatistan sample of about $12, with upscale venues higher, so I set the cocktail at $14. No reliable regular price for a glass of wine was found, so I set it from its usual price relationship to beer and cocktails. All accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge, not from searches or listings. They assume July, which is Tampa's hot, lower-demand off-season. Tampa has very few registered hostels, so the two hostel anchors are especially uncertain.
comparable_city_reasoning: I compared Tampa with other mid-sized Sun Belt US metros such as Orlando, Jacksonville and Charlotte, and with nearby St. Petersburg, FL. Restaurant and drink prices are close to the US urban average. Summer hotel rates are moderate, below the winter and spring peak.
